verdict_reason: No material contradiction or important omission was found in the complete summary against the supplied 2014 core-rule extraction. Supplementary operational clarifications are identified below as deductions rather than additional printed rules.

scope.excluded_material: No question sets, answer keys, reader outputs, grades, prior findings, browsing, prior game knowledge, or PDF evidence were used. No readers were contacted. The summary was not edited.

checked_claims.claim: 40 tokens: seven of each of five gem colors plus five gold; 90 development cards split 40/30/20; ten nobles.
Shuffle the three development decks separately; arrange by increasing level; reveal four cards per level.
Random nobles equal players plus one; unused nobles removed for the entire game; six token piles within reach.
Two-player setup has four of each gem and three nobles; three-player setup has five of each gem and four nobles; keep all gold; no other player-count changes.
Youngest player starts; turns proceed clockwise; exactly one of four actions is required.
Take three gems of different colors or two of one color only when at least four of that color remain before taking.
Gold cannot be taken through the ordinary gem-taking actions.
checked_claims.note: The source says reserving is the only way to obtain a gold token.

checked_claims.claim: Reserve one face-up card or the top card of a selected level deck without showing a blind draw.
Reservations stay in hand; maximum three; no discarding; only their holder may buy them; purchase is the only way to remove one.
Reserve gains one gold if available; an empty gold pile does not prevent reserving.
Purchase one face-up card or a card reserved on a previous turn; pay the displayed cost with applicable discounts.
Gold substitutes for a gem color; all spent gems and gold return to the central supply.
Bonuses from previously acquired development cards discount matching colors; multiple bonuses combine; sufficient bonuses can reduce token payment to zero.
Immediately replace a purchased or reserved face-up development with one from the same level; an exhausted deck leaves empty spaces.
Purchased cards are arranged by color with bonuses and prestige visible to everyone at all times.
At end of turn hold at most ten tokens including gold; return excess tokens, potentially including all newly taken tokens; tokens remain publicly visible.
Returning newly obtained reservation gold when reducing to ten is allowed.
checked_claims.note: The limit includes jokers and permits returning all or some newly drawn tokens; no gold exception is given.

checked_claims.claim: Nobles are checked at end of the active player's turn; eligibility uses at least the required card bonuses only, never tokens.
Noble visit is mandatory, not an action, limited to one per turn; choose one if several qualify; received tile goes face-up in front of the player and is worth three points.
Unchosen qualifying nobles remain available for future turns.
checked_claims.note: The source transfers only the chosen tile and supplies no removal instruction for the other revealed tiles.

checked_claims.claim: The end trigger is reaching at least fifteen prestige; finish the round so players have equal turns; highest prestige including nobles wins; tied players compare fewest purchased developments.
Reaching fifteen can mean exceeding fifteen and does not itself guarantee victory.
checked_claims.note: Points can arrive in increments; victory is decided only after the round by highest total.

checked_claims.claim: Deck or market exhaustion is not an alternative end trigger; play continues with remaining legal actions under the normal prestige trigger.
checked_claims.note: Explicitly permitted empty market spaces coexist with the sole stated prestige-based end condition. This does not establish a new pass or shortage action.

checked_claims.claim: Empty gem supplies cannot provide tokens; taking two still needs four before taking.
checked_claims.note: Physical token unavailability plus the explicit two-token threshold supports this clarification, without establishing taking fewer than three different gems.

checked_claims.claim: Discounts do not generate tokens or change; excess bonuses in one color cannot pay another color.
checked_claims.note: Bonuses are same-color discounts and payment may reach zero; the source provides no token-award or cross-color conversion procedure.

checked_claims.claim: Remaining empty market spaces stay empty after their level deck is exhausted.
checked_claims.note: The source provides no way to return acquired or reserved cards to a deck.

checked_claims.claim: The quick references preserve the main action choices, limits, component counts, setup adjustments, and final-round rule.
checked_claims.note: The brief reserve row omits the available-gold exception, but that exception appears explicitly at summary lines 87, 108 and 180; the complete summary is clear.

important_omissions_check.setup: Covered, including unused nobles, player-count token adjustments, first player and turn direction.
important_omissions_check.timing_and_actions: Covered, including mandatory one action, immediate market refill, end-of-turn token cap and noble check.
important_omissions_check.component_destinations: Covered for payments, excess tokens, purchased developments, reservations, received nobles, and removed setup nobles.
important_omissions_check.costs_and_exceptions: Covered for bonus discounts, gold substitution, free purchases, reserve cap, no discard, absent gold, and exhausted decks.
important_omissions_check.scoring_and_ending: Covered for prestige sources, fifteen-point trigger, equal-turn final round, highest total, nobles and fewest-development-card tiebreaker.
important_omissions_check.omitted_examples: The numerical card-cost and noble-qualification illustrations are not repeated verbatim, but the general rules governing them are present; the discount example is retained.

source_limitations.limitation: Some level icons and page-layout relationships are lost in the extraction. The deck names, totals and ordering remain recoverable from the surrounding text.

The extraction gives a single development-card example and generic bonus rules, but not all card-face artwork. The universally phrased one-bonus-per-card description and zero-point card description cannot be independently verified card by card from this extraction. They are consistent with its color-sorting and bonus descriptions; no contrary rule appears. Likewise, no special per-color bonus cap is stated, beyond the finite available components.

The source explicitly keeps reservations in hand and requires an unseen top-deck draw. Treating all reserved cards in hand as private, including formerly public face-up cards, is an interpretation of that hand procedure rather than an express sentence requiring every reservation to be concealed. The summary acknowledges that a face-up reserved card was already known.

Both excess-token return and noble checks are end-of-turn procedures; the source does not explicitly order them. The summary orders token return before nobles. This order cannot affect qualification because nobles use bonuses only.

The source does not establish taking fewer than three differently colored gems when fewer colors are available, an optional reduced take when more colors are available, or a pass procedure. The summary does not invent any such action.
The source supplies only the fewest-purchased-development-card tiebreaker; it does not establish how to resolve a tie that persists after it. The summary does not invent a further tiebreaker.

BGG identifier, play time, extraction/summarization dates and verification metadata are not gameplay rules and are not independently established by the supplied rule text. The 2014 copyright and named designer are present at source lines 134-147.

The cached source_pdfs/splendor-rules.pdf was identified in the assignment as a nonmatching 2024 revision and was deliberately not consulted. This audit is of the exact supplied 2014 text hash, not a PDF comparison.

The overview uses abbreviated immediate-noble/end wording. The detailed noble and end-of-game sections explicitly provide end-of-turn checks and completion of the round; the summary correctly follows those detailed provisions.

line_reference_convention: Line-number arrays are inclusive start/end pairs, flattened when multiple ranges are cited; [n,n] denotes a single line. Source references use the complete extraction numbered from line 1.
